Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman, Advocate ... For the petitioner

Mr. Mostafa Niaz Mahmood with Mr. A.Z.M. Nunil Amin, Advocate -----For the Opposite party Nos. 1 & 3.
parties:
Md. Nazib Uddin alias Nazim ... Pre-emptor-Respondent- Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Mukul Mondol and others ….Pre-emptee-Appellant …..Opposite parties
full_judgment:
07. Learned Advocate Mr. Khalilur Rahman has appeared on behalf of the petitioner. His main contention is that, the aforesaid exchange deed No. 2769, dated 28.06.2005 is not a deed of exchange. In substance the said deed is a sale deed under the garb of exchange deed. He also submits that, the pre-emptor-respondent-petitioner has proved his case by adducing oral and documentary evidence before the trial court. The trial court has rightly passed the judgment and order dated 27.05.2014, allowing the pre-emption case. He next submits that, the exchange deed was made for 7¾ decimals of land, which clearly shows that, the exchange deed is mere paper transaction. Besides, he also submits that, admittedly the pre-emptee No. 1 purchase 4½ decimals of land, on 28.06.2005, and the pre-emptee No. 1 and pre-meptee No. 2 have executed the deed of exchange No. 2769, on the following date 28.06.2005. The pre-emptee Mukul Mondal had entered into the suit property by virtue of the alleged deed of exchange without himself taking possession of 4½ decimals of land of deed No. 2769, dated 28.06.2005. This also proved that the deed in question was a mere colorable deed of exchange. The pre-emptee No.1 is a mere stranger in the suit property. He also submits that, the petitioner submitted all relevant documents including the deed of exchange, vide his examination in chief, although these deeds were not marked as exhibit by the court below. However, the trial court has taken into consideration the exchange deed No. 2769, dated 28.06.2005 and it was of the opinion that, the pre-emptor -petitioner has been able to prove his case, while it has also held that, the burden to prove the said deed of exchange was a saf-kabala. As such, the trial court has arrived at correct findings, but the appellant court, without properly appreciating the evidence on record, has wrongly sifted the burden of proof and held that the burden to prove that the deed No. 2769 dated 28.06.2005 was saf-kabala lied upon the pre-emptor and it has allowed the appeal and reversed the findings of the trial court and has set aside the judgment and order of the trial court and, thereby, the appellate court has committed error of law, that has resulted in error in the impugned decision and has also occasioned in failure of justice. He also submits that, the boundary is not specified although the suit property lying several 4 plots. He, therefore, prays that the Rule may be made absolute. 

 08. Learned Advocate Mr. Mostafa Niaz Mahmood has appeared for the pre-emptee-appellant-opposite party No. 1 and 3. He, on the other hand, submits that, the entire pleadings and the evidence on record, if considered together, then it will be evident the pre-emptor and the pre-emptee all are relatives and all are co-sharers in the suit property, but, this has not been disclosed in the application for pre-emption. He also submits that, the appellate court has rightly found that, the onus to prove that the deed of exchange No. 2769, dated 28.06.2005 was a saf-kabala was upon the pre-emptor-petitioner and that he had failed to prove that, the deed of exchange was a deed of saf-kabala. He submits that, the burden to prove that the said sub-kabala deed was clearly rested on the pre-emptor-petitioner as per provisions of section 102 of the Evidence Act, 1872 as has been rightly held by the appellate court. As regards the boundary of the suit property, the learned Advocate also submits that, this has not been agitated before the court below. Moreover, in a pre-emption case the question of boundary is not the relevant issue, rather the relevant issue is as to whether the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in the suit property and whether the petition filed under section 96(1) of SAT Act, 1950, has merit and whether the petition was barred by limitation. The trial court has found that the suit was not barred by limitation and the appellate court has also concurred with this findings. Therefore, he submits that, the other issues need not be discussed here, because the transaction done by the deed of exchange No. 2669, dated 28.06.2005 was not a sale, rather it was a deed of exchange of property between pre-emptee No. 1 and 2. Therefore, this petition filed under section 96 (1) of the SAT Act, 1950, was not competent. He concludes that, the Rule has no merit and the same is liable to be discharged. 

 14. Now in view of the provision of 102 of the Evidence Act, 1872, I am of the opinion that, the burden of proof that the deed of exchange No. 2769 dated 28.06.2005 was a deed of sub-kabala was upon the pre-emptor-petitioner and the appellate court has rightly held that this burden rests on the pre-emptor, but the pre-emptor has failed to discharge this burden. 

 18. In view of facts and circumstances of this case and in the light of the provisions of section 102 of the Evidence Act, 1872, I am of the considered opinion that, in passing the impugned judgment and order, the appellate court has committed no error of law in holding that the burden of proof that the deed of exchange No. 2769 dated 28.06.2005 was a saf-kabala rested upon the pre-emptor-petitioner and that be could not discharge his burden. Hence, the impugned decision is not erroneous, nor the same has resulted in any error of law, nor has occasioned any failure of justice.
